main_text.p: per Fatha & dualis fit numeri, scil. duæ vulpes. in versione Erpenianâ pro [super eum] lege [super illud] super Idolum scil. non super cultorem.

Prov. 85 وقع فلان في سن راسه Cecidit quidam ([ὀδόντα?]) in dentem capitis ejus. ] Lege في سي راسه vel سوا راسه quod sonare videtur, æqualem capiti mensuram, vel, illud quod caput ejus æquet. i. e. referentibus Al Jauhario & Al Firuzabadio, in عدد شعر راسه [?] tantam rerum copiam quæ numerum capil-orum capitis ejus aequet. vel juxta alios quae [illegible, ~4 letters] cum obruat, & ad caput ejus pertingat, in [illegible, ~8 letters] tantam quantam capere potest, vel quantâ uis, prosperitatem. Dicitur ergo [illegible, ~3 letters] cum quis prosperitatem seu rerum omnium abundantiam consequatur. Quod autem legunt nonnulli [illegible, ~5 letters] monet [illegible, ~3 letters] esse [illegible, ~2 letters] Erratum è literarum permutatione.

Ptov. 89. [illegible, ~9 letters] Edha zallal' alemo,'zalla bezallatin alemin . Cum errat eruditus errat errore eruditò. [illegible, ~6 letters] lege [illegible, ~4 letters] Edha zallal' alemo zalla bezallarebi alamon. Cum errat eruditus, errat errore ejus mundus. ( fc. explicante Al-Maidanio) [illegible, ~8 letters] quoniam sunt eruditi seductores qui eum imitentur. inde Poëta,

page.notes: Arabic words are printed in a small Arabic face and read with uncertainty in several places: "في سي راسه", "سوا راسه", "عدد شعر راسه" and the final Arabic phrase on the last line are marked [?]. The Greek in parentheses after "Cecidit quidam" is uncertain and marked [?]. The page continues below the cut-off, so the last line ends with a hyphen and no catchword or signature is given. Arabic words and the Arabic verse lines could not be read letter by letter, so they are marked as illegible. The reading "Ptov. 89." is doubtful and is given as printed. The "litique" catchword at the lower right is taken as printed.
